note: `referencePng` is exported by the Devup Bridge plugin when one serves the file, so a reference image no longer needs login or spends Figma allowance, and the plugin never refuses it. `get_screenshot` draws the node alone - no layer beside, above or below it - over the fills of the frames and sections it sits in and the page background, across the node's render bounds. A plugin cannot ask for that picture, so it draws the closest one over the same bounds (`useAbsoluteBounds: false`; scale 1 with the longer edge held to 8192px like the direct path's `maxDimension`, sRGB): while its ancestors make one plain colour under the node, the node alone (`contentsOnly: true`) with that colour named, the same picture; otherwise, as inside a frame painted with an image or a gradient, the area as the canvas shows it (`contentsOnly: false`) with the page background named. The bridge flattens the export onto the colour named and hands it back as the single image block `get_screenshot` gives, through the same validation. Other layers reaching into an area drawn as the canvas shows it are in that picture and not in `get_screenshot`'s; the plugin names them and the export answer carries that as `referencePngNote`, which resource delivery keeps. Measured against `get_screenshot` on fourteen nodes: the twelve drawn alone had the same sizes and differed by at most 16/255 (37/255 on a photo grid), the two drawn as the canvas shows them by at most 15/255 and 9/255, and the render harness scored each screen within 0.02 points either way. The plugin manifest declares `enablePrivatePluginApi`, which Figma requires before it fills `figma.fileKey`; builds without it reported no key. A plugin built before this devup-mcp answers `DEVUP_BRIDGE_UNKNOWN_SCRIPT`; that read, and a reference PNG over the 8 MiB one bridge answer carries (`DEVUP_REFERENCE_PNG_TOO_LARGE`, now `DEVUP_FIGMA_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE`), go to the direct path when the plugin reported the file's key, and when the direct path refuses with nothing to retry (no login) the plugin's refusal comes back with what to do instead of a login prompt. An asset too large to send says how large it was. `devup_figma_auth` no longer lists `referencePng` among what needs login. Update the plugin checkout and run the plugin again to get the new reads.
